newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - FAI mulls action against Cinema Plus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - FAI mulls action against Cinema Plus.

text.p: FAI Insurances Ltd said on Thursday it was considering legal action against Cinema Plus Ltd, a regional developer of the giant IMAX entertainment screens which plans to list on the Australian Stock Exchange.
"I am waiting for advice," FAI chief executive Rodney Adler told Reuters when asked if the company would begin legal proceedings against Cinema Plus, which plans to list October 4.
Adler said he believed the insurance company had valid claims which focussed on FAI's role in securing the site in Sydney's inner-city region of Darling Harbour.
Cinema Plus said in its float prospectus that its lawyers believed "that FAI's prospects of successfully maintaining its allegations are extremely poor".

The prospectus said FAI's lawyers had alleged in a draft claim in June this year that the insurance firm struck a deal in May 1994 to assist Cinema Plus in negotiating development approval with the state government's Darling Harbour Authority.

The draft claim, which has not been filed with the courts, also said FAI had alleged it would provide A$8.5 million in funds to Cinema Plus and take units of an equivalent amount in a trust to operate the IMAX theatre.
"If a claim is filed, Cinema Plus will defend it and does not intend to accept any liability," the prospectus said.

Cinema Plus executive vice president Gary Blom said at a news conference to announce the A$31 million sharemarket listing that the FAI claim did not seek financial damages and no negotiations were being held.
Blom, whose privately-held company will be the largest single shareholder with a 29 percent stake, said the FAI claim was related to actions by an earlier group of shareholders in Cinema Plus.
Cinema Plus will list 41.3 percent of its issued capital early next month in an underwritten offer of 31 million shares at A$1.00 each to private and institutional shares.
The offer, fully underwritten by Prudential-Bache Securities, opens for about two weeks on September 12 but is already nearly fully subscribed.

Cinema Plus has the exclusive contract for the development of the giant IMAX cinemas in Australia and New Zealand. The Sydney theatre is due to open on September 26 and will be the largest screen in the world, standing eight storeys high or 10 times larger than a normal cinema screen.
The company forecast 1996/97 after tax profit of A$2.7 million on sales of A$13.6 million, representing nine months of trading from the Sydney cinema.
Net profit is forecast to rise to A$6.4 million on sales of A$27.3 million in 1997/98, which will include an eight month contribution from a cinema in Melbourne planned to open in September 1997.
